plugin.name: NetBox Sync
plugin.description: Keep Termix hosts in sync with the devices, virtual machines and IP addresses in NetBox, filtered by tags.

tab.title: NetBox Sync
tab.loadError: Could not load the NetBox settings.
tab.notConfigured: Connect NetBox to start syncing hosts.

netboxUrl.label: NetBox URL
netboxUrl.hint: The address you open NetBox at, like https://netbox.example.com.

token.label: API token
token.hint: A read only token is enough. Create one in NetBox under your user, API Tokens.
token.saved: A token is saved. Type a new one to replace it.

caCert.label: CA certificate
caCert.hint: Only for a NetBox with a certificate from your own CA. Paste the PEM.

ipAddresses.label: IP addresses
ipAddresses.description: Sync IP addresses from IPAM, each as its own host. Addresses that are already a synced device's or VM's primary IP are skipped.

tags.label: Tags
tags.hint: NetBox tag names or slugs. Leave empty to sync every object.
tags.placeholder: Add a tag and press Enter

excludeTags.label: Skip objects with these tags
excludeTags.placeholder: Add a tag and press Enter

statuses.label: Statuses
statuses.hint: NetBox status values like active or staged. Leave empty for every status.
statuses.placeholder: Add a status and press Enter

credentialId.label: SSH key
credentialId.empty: You have no saved SSH keys.

credentialTagPrefix.label: Credential tag prefix
credentialTagPrefix.hint: A NetBox tag that starts with this, like dashlane:8A1B..., gives the host the Termix credential with the same tag, on new and existing hosts. The Dashlane plugin tags its credentials this way. Leave empty to turn it off.

folder.label: Folder name
folder.hint: Used for every host, or when the object has no value for the folder you picked.

portCustomField.label: Port custom field
portCustomField.hint: A NetBox custom field with the SSH port. Optional.

usernameCustomField.label: Username custom field
usernameCustomField.hint: A NetBox custom field with the SSH username. Optional.

copyNetboxTags.label: Copy NetBox tags
copyNetboxTags.description: Give each host the tags it has in NetBox. Tags you add in Termix are kept.

syncTag.label: Extra tag
syncTag.hint: Added to every synced host. Leave empty for none.

syncNotes.label: Write notes
syncNotes.description: Put the NetBox link and description in the host's notes.

adoptExisting.label: Link existing hosts
adoptExisting.description: When a host with the same address already exists, update it instead of adding another.

missingAction.label: When an object leaves NetBox or the filter

autoRemove.label: Remove old entries automatically
autoRemove.description: Delete a host once it has been gone from NetBox, or out of the filter, for a while. Until then it is kept or tagged as set above.

removeAfterDays.label: Remove after (days)
removeAfterDays.hint: Counted from the first sync that found it missing. 0 removes it on that sync.

autoSync.label: Sync automatically
autoSync.description: Run a sync on a schedule in the background.

forget.title: Disconnect NetBox?
forget.description: Your settings and token are removed. Synced hosts stay, but are no longer updated.

deleteHosts.title: Delete hosts?
deleteHosts.description_one: This sync deletes {{count}} host that is no longer in NetBox.
deleteHosts.description_other: This sync deletes {{count}} hosts that are no longer in NetBox.

toast.synced: Sync done: {{created}} added, {{updated}} updated, {{deleted}} removed, {{missing}} missing.

errors.invalidUrl: Enter an http or https address without a username or password.
errors.noObjectTypes: Pick at least one of devices, virtual machines or IP addresses.
errors.unauthorized: NetBox refused the token. Check that it is valid and can read devices and virtual machines.
errors.notFound: NetBox did not answer at this address. Check the URL.
errors.badResponse: NetBox sent an answer this plugin does not understand.
errors.unknownTag: NetBox has no tag {{detail}}. Use the tag's name or slug as NetBox shows it.

use.title: Use NetBox Sync
use.description: Connect NetBox and sync its devices and virtual machines into your own hosts.
